Other sources include [[Barbarian Assault/Gambles#High Gambles|high-level gambling]] at the [[Barbarian Assault]] [[Minigames|minigame]], [[Larran's big chest]], and [[Managing Miscellania]] (if residents are assigned to farming).

[[Farming runs#Herb run|Herb running]] ranarr seeds is profitable if disease chance is minimised and yield is maximised. Use [[ultracompost]], or the enhanced [[Fertile Soil]] spell, to reduce disease and increase the average yield. Plant [[Anima seed|anima seeds]], [[iasor seed|iasor]] to reduce disease chance, and [[attas seed|attas]] to increase yield. Equip the [[Farming cape]] and have [[magic secateurs]] equipped or in the inventory when harvesting to increase yield.

It is also recommended to utilise disease-free patches in five locations:
* [[Troll Stronghold (location)|Troll Stronghold]] after completing [[My Arm's Big Adventure]]
* [[Hosidius]] patch after completing the [[Kourend & Kebos Diary#Easy|easy Kourend & Kebos Diary]]
* [[Weiss]], after building the [[Fire of Nourishment]] [[fire pit]]
* [[Outer Fortis]] after obtaining 16,000 [[Glory]] at the [[Fortis Colosseum]]
* [[Harmony Island]], accessible after completing the [[Morytania Diary#Elite|Elite Morytania Diary]]

Ranarr weed has a minimum of 3 [[Farming#Variable crop yield|harvest lives]], increasing by 1 for each tier of [[compost]] used (for a maximum of 6 when using [[ultracompost]]). [[File:Spirit seed detail.png|left|150px]]
A '''spirit seed''' is a rare [[Seeds|seed]] that [[members]] can use to grow a [[spirit tree]] at level 83 [[Farming]]. Players can pay a gardener five [[monkey nuts]], one [[monkey bar]], and one [[ground tooth]] to watch over a growing spirit tree.

There are five [[Spirit Tree Patch|patches]] players can grow, one each at [[Port Sarim]], [[Etceteria]], [[Brimhaven]], [[Hosidius]], and the [[Farming Guild]] (at level 85 Farming). Players can only have one planted at 83, two at 88, three at 93, and four at 96. Upon reaching 99 Farming, the restriction is removed, and players can plant unlimited spirit trees. Players are not limited to the number of [[spirit tree sapling]]s they can own, only planted saplings based on the appropriate Farming level. A spirit tree can also be planted in a [[Player-owned house]] with level 75 [[Construction]] and does not count towards the player's tree limit. There are also eight other spirit trees which players can use, but already exist and do not need to be grown.

Spirit seeds are obtainable from [[bird nest]]s. This means it is possible for players to indirectly buy them by purchasing [[mole skin]]/[[Mole claw|claws]] from other players on the [[Grand Exchange]] and trading them to [[Wyson the gardener|Wyson]] until a spirit seed is found in a nest. They are also a potential reward for completing easy, medium, and hard [[farming contracts]] in the [[Farming Guild]] or defeating certain monsters.

[[Garden pie]]s and [[spicy stew]]s can be used to boost a player's Farming level, up to 3 levels and 5 levels respectively, allowing them to create spirit tree saplings or plant them. Boosting is required when creating the sapling and when planting the tree. It is also possible to use boosts to be able to plant more spirit trees than the player's normal Farming level allows. When boosting, note that planting the seed in the pot and planting the sapling both require 83 farming. They can both be done in one boost if timed correctly. Saplings grow on a global tick which occurs once every 5 minutes. First determine when this tick happens with a different seedling. Also, check with a different boost if the skill reduction tick isn't too close to the sapling tick. If the ticks don't overlap, you can easily grow the seedling and plant the sapling in one boost.

As there are limited spots the player can plant spirit trees, any excess spirit seeds the player has can be traded in at [[Guildmaster Jane]] for tier 5 [[Seed pack]]s which are worth an average of {{NoCoins|{{SeedPackValue|5|spiritseed=No|hespori=No}}}}. Tier 5 seed packs have an approximately 1/22 chance of containing another spirit seed which can itself be traded in for an additional pack, meaning the average value of a seed pack when trading in all spirit seeds obtained for additional packs converges to the slightly higher value of {{NoCoins|{{SeedPackValue|5|spiritseed=Yes|hespori=No}}}}.

'''Grape seeds''' can be planted in a [[vine patch]] at the [[Hosidius]] [[Vinery]] at level 36 [[Farming]] in order to grow a [[grape vine]], which will yield [[grapes]]. Grape seeds can be obtained from the [[Tithe Farm]] for 2 points per seed.

Players will need to use [[saltpetre]] on the patches with a [[gardening trowel]] in order to treat the soil before planting the grape seeds. Afterwards, [[Gallow]] will watch over your grapes for free. [[Sulphurous fertiliser]] can be used on the patches to increase the yield of [[grapes]] by roughly 180% and [[Zamorak's grapes]] by roughly 70%.

Once fully grown, players can check the grape vine's health for 625 Farming experience and can harvest the [[grapes]] (or [[Zamorak's grapes]] if players have a sufficient amount of [[Bologa's blessing]]s in their inventory). The amount of grapes harvested from a fully grown grape vine is random, much like harvesting herbs, but has a minimum number of five grapes per seed (five harvest lives). Players with higher Farming levels can expect substantially more grapes from each vine. After all the grapes have been harvested, the grape vine will die and players will have to clear the farming patch with a spade.

When fully grown, it will grow into the [[Hespori]], a [[demi-boss]] that can be defeated for 12,600 Farming experience. It is not necessary to water or [[compost]] a Hespori plant, nor does it need protection from [[Disease (Farming)|disease]]. It takes 22–32 hours to grow, depending on when it was planted. The [[shrivelled plant|flower behind the cave entrance]] will be in bloom when the Hespori plant is fully grown.
Players can speak to [[Arno]] if they wish to stop randomly receiving Hespori seeds as they harvest, clear, or check the health of their crops around Gielinor.

Hespori seeds are most commonly dropped from plants grown in [[Special patches]]; players looking to fight Hespori more often should consider growing [[Cactus (Farming)|cactus]], [[nightshade]], [[Mushroom|mushrooms]] and [[Giant seaweed|giant seaweed.]] Giant seaweed is a popular choice as the [[Seaweed spore|seaweed spores]] are easily obtainable, grow quickly, and have a 1/15 chance to drop a Hespori seed; similar to the Tangleroot, this is rolled on the last harvesting attempt.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1250152763910230018|date=14 April 2020|archiveurl=https://reldo.runescape.wiki/i/101480|archivedate=24 April 2020}}

If the player has no room in their inventory, they will not receive a Hespori seed. In most cases, the chance of receiving a Hespori seed is 500 times the base chance of the [[Tangleroot]].{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1295267912438222848|date=17 August 2020|archiveurl=https://reldo.runescape.wiki/i/107150|archivedate=21 October 2020}} At 99 Farming, the effective chance of Tangleroot per Hespori seeds received is between 1/252.2<ref>for plants with a base rate of 1/5000: hardwood, spirit, and redwood trees</ref> and 1/497.3<ref>for [[Grape vine|grape vines]] with a base rate of 1/385,426</ref>. Note this is outside [[Tithe farm]] and does not account for Hespori seeds received from [[seed pack]]s.
Unlike many other seeds, Hespori seeds cannot be used to fill [[birdhouses]].

The seed chance is rolled primarily during a patch's '''check health''' stage; if the patch does not have an option to check health, it instead rolls during the '''final''' harvest. The rates do not scale by the player's Farming level.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1324807678145765376|date=6 November 2020|archiveurl=https://archive.is/LGg4u|archivedate=6 November 2020|quote=See the pet's base chance and divide it by 500. '''Attas seeds''' are a type of [[anima seed]] requiring level 76 [[Farming]] (boostable) to plant. They are obtained exclusively from the [[Hespori]], and can only be planted in the [[anima patch]] within the intermediate tier of the [[Farming Guild]]. Planting an attas seed gives 100 [[Farming]] [[experience]].

From the moment the seed is planted, the [[attas plant]] will increase the yield of player's farming patches worldwide, by increasing the chance to save a [[Farming#Variable crop yield|harvest life]] by 5%.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1199288075186294784|date=26 November 2019|archiveurl=https://reldo.runescape.wiki/i/105451|archivedate=25 May 2020|quote=Percentage reduction on losing a life at each roll - specifically 5%.}} This effect stacks with other similar chance-to-save boosts, such as the [[magic secateurs]] and the [[Farming cape]]. The plant will provide this effect for approximately 3.5 days (8 x 640 mins) before dying. To maximise the duration of the plant's effects, it is recommended to plant it ~10 minutes after the [[Farming tick]] occurs in the following times (UTC):
*Day 1: 12:00 AM, 10:40 AM, 9:20 PM
*Day 2: 8:00 AM, 6:40 PM
*Day 3: 5:20 AM, 4:00 PM
*Day 4: 2:40 AM, 1:20 PM
The next growth stage will occur in approximately '''{{#expr:floor((640-floor(({{#time:U}} mod 38400) / 60)) / 60)}} hours and {{#expr:(640-floor(({{#time:U}} mod 38400) / 60)) mod 60}} minutes''' {{Purge|(refresh)|hover=The timer uses the clock from the site cache. Click to refresh it for a more accurate time.}}. After refreshing, when this timer indicates 10 hours and 40 minutes, this signifies a [[Farming#Growth timing|Farming tick]] just occurred. Due to the Farming tick varying between accounts, it is recommended to wait another 15 minutes, after it says 10 hours and 25 minutes.

Once the Attas plant reaches its eighth growth stage (~74 hours after planting), it will begin to take on a withered appearance, indicating the plant will die in the next growth stage, though the benefits will remain until death. In order to reap the Attas plant's benefits again, players must clear the anima patch and plant another Attas seed. The plant cannot be resurrected with the [[Resurrect Crops]] spell. Players can remove the plant before the plant dies by using a spade on the anima patch, being prompted ''"are you sure you want to dig up this patch?"''

For example, if a 20 minute growth cycle is skipped, both herb and bush patches (which advance a growth stage every 20 minutes) will skip a growth stage. Multiple growth stages can be skipped in the same Farming tick.

Kronos plant can also speed up some other processes tied to the Farming clock, such as the rate at which berries, fruit, or cactus spines regrow after they've been picked.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1108458928185245697|date=20 March 2019|archiveurl=https://reldo.runescape.wiki/i/100611|archivedate=2 May 2023|quote=[Does Kronos give a chance for berries to regrow on bushes faster once they’re been picked once, or only when the bush is initially growing?
